blocks.h2: What Does a Catch Basin Do?
blocks.body: A catch basin is a box in the ground with a grate on top. It collects rain from your yard, driveway or downspouts and sends it to a storm sewer or drainage line. The bottom of the basin is lower than the outlet pipe, so dirt and leaves settle there instead of washing into the line. Over time that sump fills up. Once it's full, debris goes into the outlet pipe, the pipe clogs and water starts pooling on the surface.

img.alt: Diagram of a catch basin showing the inlet grate, water line, sediment settling in the sump and the outlet pipe carrying water away

blocks.h2: Signs Your Catch Basin Needs Attention

tiles.body: Water that sits around the grate for hours after a storm means the basin or pipe is clogged.
If the grate is covered, water can't get in at all. In fall, this happens fast under mature trees.
Soil washing into a cracked basin leaves a dip or hole next to it.
When the basin can't take water, it runs where the yard slopes, which can be toward your foundation.

blocks.h2: Catch Basins in Arlington Heights Yards
blocks.intro: Postwar lots in Arlington Heights are mostly flat, with mature trees and long driveways. That's a lot of leaves and runoff heading for one grate.

items.body: Neighborhoods built in the 1950s and 1960s have trees that drop a heavy load of leaves every fall. A basin that's clear in September can be packed by November.
On a flat lot, water has nowhere to go if the basin is blocked. It sits in the yard and soaks into the ground next to the basement wall.
Older brick and block basins crack and shift over decades. Soil washes in, and the basin fills faster each year.

items.h3: Part of a Dry Basement Plan
items.body: A working catch basin keeps surface water away from the house, so your [sump pump](/arlington-heights/sump-pumps) doesn't have to work as hard.

blocks.h2: Catch Basin Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: How often should a catch basin be cleaned?
items.preview: At least once a year. Twice if you have big trees nearby.
items.answer: At least once a year, ideally after the leaves fall. If your yard has mature trees, a spring and fall cleaning keeps it working through storm season.

items.q: Can I clean my catch basin myself?
items.preview: You can clear the grate. Cleaning the sump and outlet takes the right tools.
items.answer: You can and should keep the grate clear of leaves. Cleaning out the sump and clearing the outlet pipe takes a vacuum or a cable, which is where we come in.

items.q: Is the catch basin in my yard my responsibility?
items.preview: If it's on your property and drains your yard, usually yes.
items.answer: If it sits on your property and handles your yard or driveway, it's usually yours to maintain. Basins in village streets are maintained by the village. If you're not sure, we can tell you where it connects.

items.q: Why does my catch basin smell?
items.preview: Standing water and rotting leaves in the sump.
items.answer: Usually standing water and rotting leaves in the bottom of the basin. A cleaning fixes it. If it smells like sewage, the basin may be connected to a sanitary line, and that needs a closer look.

items.q: How much does catch basin repair cost in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: It depends on the damage and the pipe. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on whether it needs cleaning, a new grate, wall repair or work on the outlet pipe. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
